title: R and L
what: confusing /r/ and /l/, or using a tapped or rolled r where English has an approximant
summary: The R and L distinction is often fossilized due to native language interference, making it hard to self-correct. This persistent error can obscure meaning and detract from the speaker's otherwise advanced fluency.
listenFor: Pay close attention to the precise placement and movement of your tongue when producing both the /r/ and /l/ sounds in various word positions.

contrasts.note: Distinguish the lateral /l/ from the approximant /r/.
Ensure clear articulation of /l/ vs /r/ in consonant clusters.
Practice the approximant /r/ in initial and medial positions.
Focus on the correct articulation of /l/ and /r/ in sequence.
